title: Management plane
description: south: the hosts every other objective depends on. AWX runs here, and so does the PostgreSQL it stores everything in — if this is unhealthy, nothing else can be repaired.

panels.title: Hosts reporting
panels.description: Counts hosts currently scraped. This is the first thing to read: a host that stops reporting produces ABSENCE of data, which looks the same as a broken collector. Compare against the expected count rather than trusting the number alone.

panels.title: Per host
panels.description: up, uptime and kernel. A host missing from this table entirely is more interesting than one showing 0.

panels.title: CPU steal
panels.description: The counter that mattered. On 2026-08-22 two west guests soft-locked while steal sat near zero, so steal is NOT a reliable proxy for a stalled vCPU — but sustained steal is a different and more ordinary problem (a busy hypervisor) and is worth seeing. Read a flat zero here as 'not this failure mode', never as 'the host is fine'.

panels.title: Load average (1m)
panels.description: A stalled vCPU shows up here as load climbing with no matching CPU usage, because runnable tasks pile up while nothing executes.

panels.title: Root filesystem free
panels.description: A full disk on the PostgreSQL VM degrades AWX in ways that look like AWX being broken — which is the misattribution this whole dashboard exists to prevent.

panels.title: What this dashboard cannot tell you

options.content:
**Soft lockups are not here.** node_exporter has no metric for them; the kernel taint bit and the dmesg lines are only visible on the host, which is what AWX template `[67] General: Machines: Check kernel health` reads. A stalled vCPU shows up here indirectly — as a gap in `up`, or load without CPU — and the confirmation is `[67]`.

**Absence of data is not health.** If a host disappears from these panels the collector may have died, the host may be gone, or Grafana may be rejecting writes. Grafana cannot distinguish those, which is why the dead-man's switch is a separate service.

**Retention is 14 days.** For anything older, the run ledgers in `infra-objectives/state/` are the record.

**PostgreSQL's own metrics are absent** until a read-only `pg_monitor` role exists. Disk and memory on that host are proxies, not database health.
